plan_item: 77.44.7.D / D-06 — retention status refresh invalidates an in-flight page cursor

finding.reproduction: With page 1 loaded, an older page request is left in flight and the user explicitly refreshes page 1. Before the first-page response arrives, the old next-page control remained visible/enabled with its previous cursor. A second next-page request could supersede the refresh token and append page 2 to the cleared list, omitting the first page.
finding.regression_before_fix: The new Chromium case failed before the runtime fix: expected the stale next-page control to be hidden, but it was visible.
finding.impact: Editor/admin could display an incomplete retention-request list while reporting the newly fetched page as the visible list.

fix.kind: runtime UI correctness + regression test + asset cache versioning
fix.behavior: Starting an explicit refresh clears the old cursor and hides/disables the next-page control. Only a valid first-page response exposes the new cursor; a superseded page response cannot append. The authenticated page and nested retention module use a versioned cache key.
fix.data_model: No Page Model, Save, Publish, database, storage or authorization behavior changed.
fix.open_source_review: The implementation reuses the existing native DOM controller, request-generation token and Playwright suite; no external package/code was needed or added.
